# Copilot Instructions

ASP.NET Web Forms (.NET Framework 4.7.2, C#) shopping site backed by SQL Server via ADO.NET. Single project: `Website/Website.csproj` in `Website.sln`.

## Build / run / test

- Windows + Visual Studio (2019+): open `Website.sln`, restore NuGet, build (`Ctrl+Shift+B`), run with IIS Express (`F5`, `https://localhost:44337/`). CLI equivalent: `nuget restore Website.sln` then `msbuild Website.sln`.
- There are no tests. CI runs on every PR to `main` (all workflows in `.github/workflows/`, actions pinned to commit SHAs, top-level `permissions: {}`): CodeQL (`security-and-quality`), SBOM (Syft + GitHub dependency-graph SBOM with retries, Grype, attestation), Dependency Review, Lint, Scorecard, and `建置`. `build.yml` restores NuGet on `windows-latest`, stamps `AssemblyInformationalVersion`, publishes with MSBuild WebPublish, uploads `site.zip`, then produces a package SBOM on Ubuntu. `main` is protected by a ruleset: PR required (squash only, 0 approvals), required checks `建置`/`CodeQL`/`相依套件審查`/`Lint`, CodeQL merge protection for new High+ alerts, and required review-thread resolution. CodeQL PR review comments create threads even for note-level findings; fixing the alert auto-resolves them, otherwise they must be resolved before merge. `demo/pre-implementation` is a locked snapshot for demos — never push to it.
- Lint locally before pushing: `npx -y markdownlint-cli2@0.22.0 '**/*.md'` (config `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`, MD013 off), `editorconfig-checker` (`.editorconfig`: VS files UTF-8 BOM + CRLF, `.config`/`.sql` CRLF, everything else UTF-8 + LF), and `actionlint`. CRLF file types are `-text` in `.gitattributes` so Git stores them byte-for-byte.
- The project builds after NuGet restore on Windows/MSBuild. All runtime settings come from environment variables: `Web.config` uses Configuration Builders (`EnvironmentConfigBuilder`, `mode="Token"`) on `connectionStrings` and `appSettings`, so values are `${NAME}` tokens (`SQL_SERVER`, `SQL_DATABASE`, `SQL_ENCRYPT`, `SQL_USER`/`SQL_PASSWORD`, `SQL_MIGRATOR_USER`/`SQL_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_*`, `STORAGE_BLOB_ENDPOINT`, `STORAGE_CONTAINER`, `IMAGE_BASE_URL`). `Global.asax` runs `Website.Config.AppSettings.Validate()` and then `Website.Data.DatabaseMigrator.Run()` at startup, and returns 500 for every request if a token is unresolved or a migration fails. Add new settings as tokens read through `AppSettings`; never commit real connection strings or passwords.
- `iTextSharp` is managed by NuGet (`iTextSharp` 5.5.13.6 with `BouncyCastle.Cryptography` 2.6.2). `profile.aspx.cs` uses `iTextSharp.text`, `iTextSharp.text.html.simpleparser.HTMLWorker`, and `iTextSharp.text.pdf` for the PDF order invoice.
- NuGet uses `packages.config` + `HintPath` references (old-style csproj). The Azure SDK closure (Azure.Storage.Blobs, Azure.Identity, dbup-sqlserver) was resolved for net472 with a throwaway SDK-style project; when adding or upgrading packages, regenerate `Web.config` `runtime/assemblyBinding` redirects the same way and keep the `netstandard` entry under `compilation/assemblies`. Product images are uploaded by `Website.Data.ImageStore` to Blob container `products` (`<seller>/<guid>.<ext>`, managed identity via `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`; Azurite when the endpoint is loopback) and `pimage` stores the full URL.
- `Website.csproj` includes `Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs`, `css\style.css`, `Config\AppSettings.cs`, `Data\Db.cs`, `Data\DatabaseMigrator.cs`, `Data\ImageStore.cs`, `Data\CartSession.cs`, `Data\UserAccounts.cs`, `Data\PasswordHasher.cs`, `Data\PasswordResets.cs`, `Global.asax`, the `Migrations\*.sql` `EmbeddedResource` items and `img\products\demo_seller\*.png`. `.gitignore` excludes `bin/`, `obj/`, `packages/` (restored by NuGet) and `*.user`; `Website.csproj.user` is untracked, so the root URL relies on `Web.config`'s `system.webServer/defaultDocument` (`index.aspx`) — keep it. Some tracked product images (`apple.png`, `appol.png`, `img2.png`, `products/human99/laptop.png`) are not listed as `<Content Include>` in `Website.csproj`.
- Azure deployment (plan milestones in `Plan.md`; M1–M6 done) targets App Service (Windows) + Azure SQL in resource group `rg-shopping` (East Asia, subscription BD-CIS-Testing). One-time setup is done by the idempotent `infra/bootstrap.sh` (bash + az + gh): OIDC deploy identity `gh-shopping-deploy`, user-assigned identities `id-shopping-web` / `id-shopping-deployscript` with data-plane roles on the RG, and GitHub Environment `azure` (vars `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP`, `SQL_ADMIN_LOGIN`; secret `SQL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; allowed refs `main` and `refs/pull/*/merge`). Jobs that log in to Azure must declare `environment: azure` and `id-token: write`, and skip fork PRs. The repo uses GitHub's immutable OIDC subject `repo:jeff1121@12440417/Shopping-Website@1395787848:environment:azure`. The subscription Owner is ABAC-restricted, so Bicep must **not** create role assignments; reference the pre-created identities with `existing` instead (ADR-0004). `azure-oidc-check.yml` verifies login. Infrastructure is `infra/main.bicep` + `infra/modules/*.bicep` (param file `main.bicepparam` reads `SQL_ADMIN_LOGIN`, `SQL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_USER_NAME` from environment variables via `readEnvironmentVariable`); `infra.yml` runs lint + what-if (PR comment) on PRs and deploys on `main`. Resource names use `take(uniqueString(resourceGroup().id), 6)` as suffix. The `sql-users` deploymentScript (`infra/scripts/sql-users.ps1`) creates `shopping_app`/`shopping_migrator` with passwords stored only in Key Vault. `infra/smtp-setup.sh` (run once after the first infra deploy) creates the ACS SMTP Entra app, custom role, SMTP username and Key Vault secret `smtp-password`, then sets Environment variable `SMTP_USER_NAME`; `SMTP_USER`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` app settings are only emitted when that variable is non-empty. In PowerShell deployment scripts use `Write-Host` (not `Write-Output`) inside functions that return values. Validate locally with `az bicep build`/`az bicep lint`; a local `az deployment group what-if` needs a throwaway `SQL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env var. Never put passwords or client secrets in the repo, chat, issues or PRs.
- `deploy.yml` (push `main` except infra/docs-only changes, or `workflow_dispatch` with optional `run-id` for rollback) calls `build.yml`, uploads `Website/img/products/demo_seller/*` to Blob `products/demo_seller` (`--auth-mode login`), runs `az webapp deploy --type zip`, then `.github/scripts/smoke-test.sh` (retries; checks pages and a Front Door image). On smoke failure it redeploys the last successful run's `site` artifact. A separate job runs ZAP Baseline (rules in `.zap/rules.tsv`, report artifact only). `infra/modules/availability.bicep` adds a standard availability test and metric alert; an action group is created only when GitHub variable `ALERT_EMAIL` is set. App `Trace` output reaches Log Analytics (`AppServiceAppLogs`) only via the `AzureMonitorTraceListener` inserted by `Web.Release.config` (the assembly exists only on App Service — never add it to `Web.config`) plus the site diagnostic setting; the Application Insights codeless agent does not collect `Trace`.
- Database schema is applied at startup by DbUp (ADR-0002): `DatabaseMigrator` takes an `sp_getapplock` lock on a `migratorConnectionString` connection (capture `SqlConnection.ConnectionString` before `Open()` — afterwards the password is stripped), then runs embedded `Website/Migrations/NNNN_*.sql` scripts in name order (one transaction each, journal `dbo.SchemaVersions`, variable `$IMAGE_BASE_URL$`). `0001` creates tables idempotently (`IF OBJECT_ID ... IS NULL`); `0002`–`0004` seed categories, demo users `demo_customer`/`demo_seller` (public demo password `Demo@1234` stored as plaintext, upgraded to a hash on first login; seller `uid` 5001) and 4 demo products; `0005` widens `password` to `VARCHAR(200)` and adds `violet_password_reset`. To add a migration, add a new numbered `.sql` file (CRLF, no BOM), register it as `<EmbeddedResource>` in `Website.csproj`, and lint with sqlfluff (`--dialect tsql`); never edit an already-applied script. `db/cleanup/remove_demo_data.sql` removes demo data manually (M8).
- Full setup steps and troubleshooting live in `QuickStart.md`; `README.md` is the zh-TW project overview.

## Conventions

- Docs (including README), code comments, commit messages and PR titles/descriptions are all written in Traditional Chinese (zh-TW); only code identifiers stay in English. Domain terms are defined in `CONTEXT.md`, architecture decisions in `docs/adr/`, and the CI/CD + Azure deployment plan in `Plan.md`. Every class, method and field in code-behind has a zh-TW `/// <summary>`; every `.aspx` has a `<%-- --%>` purpose comment on line 2. Designer files also carry zh-TW field comments in the form `型別「ID」：用途` — Visual Studio regeneration reverts them to English, so restore them before committing. Keep this when adding code.
- The repo lives at `https://github.com/Jeff1121/Shopping-Website` (forked from `DarylFernandes99/Shopping-Website`).
- Encoding/line endings follow `.editorconfig`: `.cs`/`.aspx`/`.csproj`/`.sln` are UTF-8 with BOM + CRLF, `.config`/`.sql` are CRLF, everything else (Markdown, YAML, shell, Bicep) is UTF-8 + LF.

## Architecture

- Each page is a trio: `page.aspx` (markup), `page.aspx.cs` (code-behind, namespace `Website`, class = page name), `page.aspx.designer.cs` (control fields — keep in sync when adding/removing `runat="server"` controls). New files must also be registered in the old-style `Website.csproj`; new `.cs` files require `<Compile Include>` entries, and page code-behind/designer files need `DependentUpon`.
- There is **no master page**: the header/nav, logout button, cart icon and `countItems` badge are duplicated in every `.aspx`. Most `Page_Load` handlers repeat the same "if logged in, show profile/cart icons and set the badge from `Session["count"]`" block; the badge is always `countItems.Text = CartSession.Count(Session).ToString();`. Exceptions: `login.aspx.cs` (no header-state work) and `sellerProfile.aspx` (plain anchor icons in markup). Shared UI/nav changes must be applied to every page.
- Styling: `Website/css/style.css` provides minimal shared defaults; most layout remains in per-page inline `<style>` blocks.
- Two data-access styles coexist:
  - Declarative `asp:SqlDataSource` in markup using `<%$ ConnectionStrings:cmpConnectionString %>` (product list/search/sort/category in `index.aspx`, `categories.aspx`, order history and seller product edit/delete in `profile.aspx`). `index.aspx.cs` swaps the DataList's source among `SqlDataSource1..5`; `categories.aspx` links to `index.aspx?category=<name>`.
  - Imperative SQL in code-behind goes only through `Website.Data.Db` (`Query` → `DataTable`, `Execute` → rows affected, `Scalar` (DBNull → null), `Param` (null → DBNull), `GetUname(login)`; `CreateConnection()` reads `cmpConnectionString`). Pages have no `con` fields and never use `new SqlConnection`/`SqlCommand`. All SQL is parameterized and every INSERT lists its columns — never concatenate values into SQL . Account creation, login (`UserAccounts.Authenticate`) and uid assignment are in `Website.Data.UserAccounts`. Passwords are PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes (`Website.Data.PasswordHasher`, format `PBKDF2-SHA256$iterations$salt$hash`); legacy plaintext passwords are upgraded on successful login, so never compare `password` directly. Forgot-password emails a one-time link to `resetPassword.aspx?token=` (`Website.Data.PasswordResets`: only the token's SHA-256 is stored, 30-minute expiry, single use); SMTP failures show a message and log only the exception type and status code.
  - Every submit handler starts with `if (!Page.IsValid) return;` so validators also run server-side. Expected SQL failures are caught with `Db.IsDuplicateKey`/`Db.IsTruncation` (`UserAccounts.Create` returns `CreateResult`) instead of surfacing as 500s. `Global.asax.cs` `Application_Error` logs unhandled exceptions (path, type, stack — no query string or message) to Trace.
  - Seller-only pages check `UserAccounts.IsSellerLogin(Session["user"])` in `Page_Load` (`addProducts`) or `IsSeller(uid)` (`profile`, `sellerProfile`). `profile.aspx` `SqlDataSource2` scopes select/update/delete to `Session["uname"]`. Uploads must pass `ImageStore.IsSupportedExtension`, `MaxBytes` (2 MB) and `HasValidSignature` (magic bytes).

### Session state (implicit cross-page contract)

- `Session["user"]` – the login text (username **or** email); queries resolve it with `WHERE username=@x OR email=@x`. Logout sets it to `null`.
- `Session["uname"]` – the user's full name (`uname`), which is the actual PK/FK stored in cart, order and product rows. Set by `login` and `sellerSignIn`.
- `Session["count"]` – the cart as a `DataTable`, always accessed through `Website.Data.CartSession` (`Key`, `CreateTable`, `Get`, `Count`, `GrandTotal`, `LoadFromDatabase`). Columns `sno, pimage, pname, price, quantity, total, uname`, where the `uname` column holds the **seller** name (`violet_cart.sname`). Its row count drives the cart badge. Rebuilt from `violet_cart` at login (`login`/`sellerSignIn`) and cleared after checkout.
- `Session["addproduct"]` – `"<quantity>:<pname>"` written by Add-to-Cart in `index.aspx.cs` only after that quantity was reserved, before redirecting to `cart.aspx?id=<url-encoded pname>&quantity=<n>`; `cart.aspx` adds the item only when the query string matches this value exactly, then sets it to `null`.

### Cart / stock / order flow

Stock in `violet_products` is reserved atomically on add-to-cart (`index.aspx.cs`, login required; guests are redirected to `login.aspx`: `UPDATE ... SET stock = stock - @q WHERE ... AND stock >= @q`), rebalanced on quantity edit (`stock + old - new`, guarded `>= 0`; the old quantity comes from the cart row) and restored on delete (`cart.aspx.cs`). Cart rows live in both the session `DataTable` and `violet_cart` (with `sno` renumbered on delete; re-adding a product updates the existing row). Checkout (`checkout.aspx.cs`) inserts rows into `violet_order`, deletes the user's `violet_cart` rows and clears `Session["count"]`. New products from `addProducts` start with stock 0; sellers set stock via the `profile.aspx` product grid.

## Database schema caveats

`DbSql.sql` is out of date relative to the code (and has a `CREATE DATABSE` typo); the authoritative schema is `Website/Migrations/0001_create_tables.sql`. The code actually expects:

- `violet_user_login` (14 columns): `uname, email, username, password, phone, dob, country, state, city, gender, address, secq, seca, uid`. Roles are encoded in `uid`: `UserAccounts.GenerateUid` assigns 1–4998 for `register` and 5001–9999 for `sellerRegister`; `uid > 5000` (`UserAccounts.IsSeller`) means seller (checked in `profile`/`sellerProfile`, kept in ViewState across postbacks).
- `violet_products`: `pname, price, pimage, category, uname, keywords, stock` — the seller link column is `uname`, not `sname`.
- `violet_cart`: `uname` (buyer), `sno, pimage, pname, price, quantity, total, sname` (seller).
- `violet_order`: `uname, pname, orderID, orderDate, quantity, total`.
- `violet_categories` (`name`, `cimage`) — seeded by `0002`; names must match the hard-coded list in `addProducts.aspx.cs`.
- `violet_contact`: `uname, email, message`.
- Seller pages (`sellerRegister`, `sellerSignIn`, `sellerProfile`) read/write `violet_user_login`; `violet_seller_login` is unused by code.

When changing the schema, add a new migration script and update the README schema section (and `QuickStart.md` §3 if setup changes).
